title: Edge0-145B: Running Frontier AI on Private Infrastructure
summary: Edge0-145B enables high-performance generative AI tasks on hardware with limited memory. You can determine if this architecture fits your deployment.
body_markdown:
## Why local LLMs change the automation landscape


Decoupling automation throughput from the variable pricing models of cloud providers is the primary advantage of local execution. This ensures that scaling a workflow does not create an unpredictable financial liability.


By moving the inference engine inside the corporate firewall, teams eliminate the trade-off between using a high-reasoning model and maintaining a sustainable budget.


### Eliminating per-token costs in high-volume workflows


Running frontier-grade models locally transforms the operational expense of automation into a predictable capital investment in hardware.


In traditional cloud deployments, every step of a multi-agent chain (from initial summarization to final code generation) incurs a per-token fee. This means a recursive debugging loop or a high-density data ingestion task can trigger an unexpected billing spike.


> Running frontier-grade models locally transforms the operational expense of automation into a predictable capital investment in hardware.


While many vendors monetize control by stripping features from self-hosted builds, Activepieces provides the same SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, and secret management in its air-gapped edition as it does on the managed cloud.


Regulated organizations like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run this build in production because air-gapped deployment delivers the full enterprise control plane rather than a fraction of it.


### Edge0-145B data residency and compliance


For strict regulatory frameworks like PIPEDA or FISMA, local deployments provide a definitive solution by ensuring that sensitive telemetry and PII never traverse the public internet.


While cloud providers offer "zero-retention" tiers, these often require specialized enterprise contracts and still involve a third-party processor handling the data in transit.


The following transition illustrates the fundamental shift in data gravity as high-parameter local models become viable.


Intelligence is no longer a centralized resource, but a localized utility that resides where the data is generated.


Consequently, an organization can automate workflows involving sensitive medical records or proprietary trade secrets without needing to audit the data-handling practices of an external LLM vendor.


This total control over the inference environment means that security teams can apply existing network isolation and air-gapping protocols to their AI infrastructure, satisfying compliance requirements that previously blocked the adoption of cloud-based reasoning engines.
